query: I am moving to Finland on a 5-month temporary contract. Do I have to pay tax on my global income to Finland, or only on my Finnish salary?
expected_answer: Since your stay in Finland is 6 months or less, you are treated as a nonresident (limited tax liability) taxpayer. You are only liable to pay tax to Finland on income earned from Finnish sources (such as your Finnish salary). You do not pay tax to Finland on your global income.

query: I just got hired by a Finnish company but haven't delivered my tax card yet. Is it true that they will deduct 60% of my wages as tax?
expected_answer: Yes. Under Finnish tax regulations, if you do not present a valid tax card (verokortti) to your employer before your wages are paid, they are legally required to withhold a flat 60% of your wages as tax. You should apply for a tax card as soon as you receive your Finnish personal identity code.

query: I am relocating to Finland for a specialist role with a monthly salary of 6,000 euros. What is the special tax rate for foreign key employees in 2026?
expected_answer: As of 1 January 2026, the tax-at-source rate for foreign key employees is 25% (reduced from 32% under previous laws). To qualify, you must have a monthly cash salary of at least EUR 5,800, become a resident taxpayer when starting work, have special expertise, and have not been a resident taxpayer in Finland during the preceding 5 calendar years.

query: I got a job on a construction site in Helsinki. My supervisor told me I need a tax number. How do I get one, and do I need to register it?
expected_answer: Yes. Everyone working on a construction site or a shipyard in Finland must wear an ID badge showing an individual tax number (veronumero). You must first obtain a Finnish personal identity code. Once you have it, you or your employer can request that your tax number be entered into the public Register of Tax Numbers before you begin working on-site.

query: I am coming to Finland for 3 months to work on a farm. Will I be taxed at a flat 35% rate, or can I choose a different tax option?
expected_answer: By default, seasonal workers staying 6 months or less are taxed at a flat tax-at-source rate of 35%. However, you have the option to apply for progressive tax treatment. Under progressive taxation, your tax percentage is calculated based on your estimated total annual income, which often yields a much lower tax rate if your seasonal earnings are modest.

query: I am an international student working part-time. If I receive a student financial aid from Kela, is that money taxable in Finland?
expected_answer: Yes. If you receive Finnish financial aid (such as a study grant) from Kela, that income is subject to Finnish taxes. If you also work, your student financial aid and earned wage income are combined to calculate your progressive tax rate, and you must apply for a tax card that accounts for both sources.
